# COMPARTMENT STANDALONE VALIDATION PLAN
**`ffn_cellsim` · drafted 2026-07-25 · branch `codex/ff-ac-codex` · design only, no code changed**

Ten tracks were designed against the PI specification, four were adversarially attacked, and a completeness critic reviewed the whole. This document is the merged result. Where an attacker corrected a design I use the corrected version and say so in-clause; every gate an attacker showed to be tautological has been deleted rather than weakened.

---

## 0. The gate has changed

**Mechanical connectedness of every part is the gate. Physiological magnitude is not.** Every gate in this document is therefore a conservation identity, an exact zero/non-zero, a sign-sense, a symmetry, a scaling exponent, a grid-invariance, an analytic-oracle *ratio*, or an ablation ordering — never a comparison of an absolute value against a literature band. A gate that cannot be evaluated without an unsourced constant does not appear. Parameters must still be plausible enough not to blow up numerically, and are swept coordinates or fitted **outputs**, never inputs to a pass criterion.

**Labelling rule, mandatory on every artifact.** Each run emits one JSON with: config + config hash; population census (unique active IDs per component, dormant capacity, node/element counts, exact peak GPU bytes); a **t0 row measured before the first step**; per-step telemetry; residual **and** residual/signal; per-parameter provenance (`SOURCED` / `DERIVED` / `PI_GAP` / `UNRATIFIED_PROXY`); the **measured** evidence rung (never a literal — `scripts/ac_gate_b_cortex_motor_native.py:393` currently hard-codes `"evidence": "CONNECTED"` and that must be deleted); and `quantitative_claim_status: BLOCKED` on every magnitude. Verdicts are `MECHANISM PASS` / `MECHANISM FAIL` / **`VOID`** (emitted, never PASS or FAIL, when residual/signal exceeds a ceiling declared *before* the run). Every gate ships a named negative control that must be **observed to fail**; a control that was never run invalidates the claim.

**One rung is missing from the ladder.** The 8-state ladder has no state for "mechanically connected, quantitatively blocked" — which under the new priority is the *success* case. PI decision D1 (§6).

---

## 1. Per-compartment tracks

**Reordering, and why.** Tracks are ordered by dependency, not PI numbering. Two new tracks (T0 instrumentation, T1 coupled solve) come first because six of the original ten have primary gates that are *unfalsifiable* without them: a non-converged component-split iteration produces the same signature as a dead connector (39.8 nm vs 0.0 nm), so every transmission gate would read ambiguous. T2 (array ownership) is third because 7 of the 32 connectors terminate on the cortex and are structurally unverifiable while it is a bind-target port. ECM (T9) precedes adhesion (T10), breaking the T8⇄T10 cycle the critic found. Protrusion (T11) is new and precedes the migration gate. Speed (T12) is split: a profiler+A/B slice lands now, the rest post-assembly.

Original PI numbering → this document: T1→**T4**, T2→**T3**, T3→**T8**, T4→**T7**, T5→**T6b**, T6→**T5**, T7→**T6a**, T8→**T10**, T9(cadherin/FAK)→§2b, T10→**T9**, T11→**T12**.

- `ac/engine/transaction.py:129` step 3 is `solve()`, a caller-supplied `Callable[[], None]`. `CellTransaction` owns no solver by design.
- `scripts/ac_gate_b_composed_native.py:232` passes `accepted_d = ones(1)` with no ledger/`tol_sq_d` — the composed cell unconditionally accepts a state in which nothing moved. (`transaction.py:139-146` already *supports* `ledger.balance_ok_d`; nothing uses it.)

### T2 — Array ownership seam: component-private arrays + driver omit-mask
*A5000. PI-gated (§6 D2).*

**Today.** `ac/cell/driver.py:141 _accumulate_all(cell, pos, f)` has **no** `omit` parameter — the only "omit" is build-time CLI (`:1288-1312 --no-myosin/--no-nucleus/--no-membrane`), which cannot hand one component to the engine while keeping the rest. Four original tracks declared this a HARD blocker with zero owners. `ac/engine/surface_body.py:349-353` contains the membrane/cortex anti-aliasing guard and is **never constructed outside tests**, so the guard has never executed. `INTEGRATION_surface_body.md:22-39` lists five un-done steps assigned to "the Lead," not to a track.

**Steps.** (i) Add the additive `omit=` mask to `_accumulate_all` with a bit-identical default. (ii) Give **cortex, membrane, nucleus** component-private `position_d`/`force_d`; construct `SurfaceBody` for real. (iii) Enforce `_storage_key` exclusivity across *all* registered components, and print distinct `.ptr` values into every artifact.

**Pass criterion.** With the mask on, engine-owned channel forces equal the incumbent's contribution node-by-node to <1e-12 relative (pure refactor parity, no physics change); pointer-identity holds for every pair; `hot_loop_dtoh_copies == 0` with the existing positive control (`driver.py:1059-1080`, gate at `:1201`) firing.

**Negative control.** Leave the mask **off** while the engine owner is bound — parity must FAIL with an exact factor-2, proving the double count is detectable and not silently absorbed. Second: alias the arrays back onto `cell.pos_d` — the guard must raise. Third: keep distinct arrays but leave mechanics as `NoOpSurfaceMechanics` — the manifest gate must FAIL with *"channels launched by `ac.cell.driver._accumulate_all`"*, catching the passenger pattern.

**Why this is high-rank.** Seven of the 32 connectors terminate on the cortex (`membrane_erm_cortex`, `surface_porous_transfer`, `sf_cortex_transient`, `mt_cortex_capture`, `lamellipodium_cortex_seam`, `filopodium_cortex_root`, `nmii_cortex_motor`). Also note: **ERM areal density is currently a mesh knob** (`erm_density_per_um2=None` → one tether per membrane vertex → ρ₀ = f(subdivisions), ~58/µm² at subdiv 6 vs ~927 at subdiv 8 against a sourced ~100/µm²; `ac/cell/compartments.py:116 linc_per_node=1` has the identical defect for LINC and was named nowhere). ## 2. Direct answers to the PI three questions

### (a) Ion channels — NOT NOW for mechanics, with five named triggers

**Position: no.** Aquaporin water permeability is *legitimately* lumpable into L_p, and this is categorically different from the lumpings the project forbids. Bell-Evans-vs-Metropolis, Hill-vs-linear-stall and Stam-Hocky-vs-2-head-spring each destroy a **discrete, force-dependent, load-bearing** mechanism. Aquaporin bears no load, is not force-gated in the mechanical range, and enters the mechanics only through the scalar areal flux — nothing downstream can distinguish 10⁴ channels each passing J/10⁴ from a uniform L_p. L_p is a constitutive coefficient, not a proxy for a mechanism.

What *is* missing is one rung **down** in the dependency order: the conserved pools N_i with per-solute σ_i and the live device enclosed volume (T6a-V2/V3). Pools are **state**; channels are the **rate law** that changes that state. Building channels before the pool exists gives a rate law with no conserved quantity to act on — structurally the same error as a load path that sums to zero. And in the ratified baseline (adherent, in medium, r = 1, quasi-static) ion fluxes are at homeostatic steady state, so their net contribution to ΔΠ_eff is a **constant** — which is exactly the constant Π₀ already ratified as a sweep axis. Adding channels now introduces conductances, densities and pump stoichiometries that are all PI-GAPs, lowering the sourced fraction of the model while changing no mechanical prediction.

**One correction the attacks forced:** turgor-setting *is* already in the mechanical load path via the constant Π₀ pressing the cell onto the coat, so it must appear as a declared channel in the T0.3 force manifest and in T10-A0's confound audit — it cannot be omitted from the adherent baseline on the grounds that channels are deferred. `ff/piezo.py` stays a **read-only reporter** wired to the membrane tension the model already computes, with `CA_FEEDBACK_GAIN = 0.0` (its own guard catches the pN/nm-vs-pN/µm unit trap, so it also serves as a zero-cost units cross-check).

### (c) Stokes vs Darcy — a staged verdict, and the drag term that must die in the same commit

**The physics.** The Brinkman screening length is ℓ_B = sqrt(k). At the project's k = 5e-18 m² (`ac/fluid/params_i0b1.yaml`), ℓ_B = 2.24 nm; re-derived from the project's own cortex population (70,686 × 3 µm over a 706.9 µm² × 0.2 µm shell ⇒ ρ_L = 1500 µm/µm³ ⇒ ξ = 25.8 nm, k = ξ²/C for C = 16–72), ℓ_B = 3.0–6.5 nm. The viscous term beats the Darcy term only below ℓ_B: the ratio is exactly (ℓ_B/L)², i.e. 2.0e-5 at L = 0.5 µm and 8.9e-8 at L = 7.5 µm. **At the whole-cell scale Darcy is not a convenience approximation of Stokes — it is the leading-order asymptotic limit of Stokes in this medium.** Re is 1.5e-10 (bulk η) to 1e-5 (pore η), so Stokes is exactly the right physics and the whole question is discretisation and cost.

**The cost.** A resolved whole-cell DNS needs ~4.2e11 cells at dx = 2 nm ≈ 25 TB for 15 fp32 fields — ~1580× a 16 GB A5000 and ~300× a full 8×H100 node. **Infeasible by construction, not merely expensive.** Whole-cell Stokes–**Brinkman** at 100–250 nm is affordable (0.2 GB, 8–130 ms/outer step) but, per the attack, **ℓ_B is unresolved there** ((dx/ℓ_B)² ≈ 2000 at dx = 100 nm), so its advertised gains — real shear, vorticity, no-slip — are grid artifacts at that resolution. Pore-scale DNS in a 0.5–1 µm REV **is** affordable (0.9–3.0 GB) and is where the one genuinely lumped number gets de-lumped.

**Verdict and staged path.** (1) **REV DNS to measure k_ij and φ from the project's own explicit filament geometry**, turning both from PI-GAP *inputs* into measured *outputs* — this directly serves PI purpose #5 and is the fine-grained move. (2) **Stokes–Brinkman only where free fluid actually exists**: the extracellular **media** the baseline specifies (today there is none at all), the cell–substrate lubrication film, bleb interiors, the perinuclear gap — regions where k→∞, ℓ_B→∞, and Darcy is not an approximation but simply wrong, and where the oracles are exact (6πμav, Brenner wall correction). (3) **Do not** attempt full-cell resolved DNS. (4) Any whole-cell Brinkman operator must carry the **storage + α div(v_s)** continuity, not div v = 0.

Volume exchange: **fully delivered**, not a Darcy deficit. Drag on filaments: **not delivered** — the only fluid→solid force is −α∇p, so a filament moving through quiescent uniform-pressure fluid feels exactly zero fluid force. Getting fluid-borne drag does **not** require resolved Stokes: the Darcy-consistent form is the Brinkman body force (μ/k)(v_f − v_s) at Darcy cost, and its coefficient is exactly what the REV can **measure**.

## 7. Honest risks

**Load paths that sum to zero — the enumerated list.** This is the failure class most likely to make a passing gate meaningless, and it has a *specific* form in almost every track:

1. **Bipolar minifilament** (T7) — net force is zero **by construction**, so any net-force metric is guaranteed zero and proves nothing. Mitigation: the cancellation ledger (anchor reaction ÷ Σ\|f_head\| per filament), reported per step.
2. **Isotropic osmotic traction** (T6a-V8) — a radial traction's vector sum is **exactly** zero by symmetry, so a net-force-only gate passes on a completely disconnected build. Mitigation: the anti-vacuity control that *demonstrates* the degenerate variant passing.
3. **MT aster and IF cage** (T8) — both radially symmetric, so a radial load transmits per-edge and cancels globally, exactly as the crawl traction did. Mitigation: \|Σf\| **and** Σ\|f\| reported separately; symmetric-load control on every drag gate.

ION CHANNELS — approve the recommendation? My defensible answer is NO, not for mechanics now, and here is the reasoning. Aquaporin water permeability is LEGITIMATELY lumpable into L_p, and this is categorically different from the lumpings the project forbids: Bell-Evans-vs-Metropolis, Hill-vs-linear-stall, and Stam-Hocky-vs-2-head-spring all destroy a discrete, FORCE-DEPENDENT, LOAD-BEARING mechanism, whereas aquaporin bears no load, is not force-gated in the mechanical range, and enters the mechanics only through the scalar areal flux — nothing downstream can distinguish 10^4 channels each passing J/10^4 from a uniform L_p. So L_p is a constitutive coefficient, not a proxy for a mechanism. What is genuinely missing is one rung DOWN in the dependency order: the conserved pools N_i with per-solute sigma_i and the live enclosed volume V. Pools are STATE; channels are the RATE LAW that changes that state. Building channels before the pool exists would give a rate law with no conserved quantity to act on — structurally the same error as a load path that sums to zero. And in your current baseline (adherent, in medium, r = 1, quasi-static) ion fluxes are at homeostatic steady state by definition, so their net contribution to dPi_eff is a constant — which is exactly the constant Pi_0 you just ratified as a sweep axis. Adding channels now would introduce conductances, densities and pump stoichiometries that are all PI-GAPs, lowering the sourced fraction of the model while changing no mechanical prediction. Keep `ff/piezo.py` as a READ-ONLY reporter wired to the membrane tension the model already computes, with CA_FEEDBACK_GAIN at 0. TRIGGERS to add them, proposed as a contract: T1 any claim involving ACTIVE volume regulation (the oracle's R != 0) — passive water flux cannot produce recovery, recovery requires N_i to change; T2 permeant-vs-impermeant discrimination (mannitol vs glycerol), which needs per-solute sigma_i plus a solute permeation pathway; T3 the inference platform treating ion homeostasis as a CELL-STATE axis (same MCF7 in DMEM vs Krebs at matched osmolality, or a transporter-inhibitor perturbation) — then the channel is the inferred object and must be explicit; T4 a mechanosensitive channel asked to CLOSE A MECHANICAL LOOP (tension -> Ca -> contractility), at which point it bears causal weight on force and must be fine-grained, with conductance/density/Ca-gain sourced FIRST; T5 the hypotonic/lysis limit where the volume trajectory is bounded by channel-mediated efflux rather than by V_b. ANTI-TRIGGER: wanting a 'more realistic' cytoplasm, or trying to fix an absolute Pi_0 — that is a magnitude problem you have explicitly deprioritised, and channels are the most expensive possible way to adjust a scalar. When they do come, they come as rate-conditioned transporter EVENTS on the conserved pool under the accepted-step transaction (the clutch / monomer-flux discipline), never as a continuum current density. Please ratify or amend T1-T5.

pi_questions: HARDWARE — probably the single largest lever in this track and not mine to decide. The solver is f64 everywhere (verified: 215 float64 sites in implicit_mechanics.py alone; the only f32 is the pruning-only hash-grid index). The RTX A5000 is GA102, which runs f64 at 1/64 of f32 (~0.43 TFLOPS f64, 768 GB/s, 16 GB); an A100 runs f64 at 1/2 (~9.7 TFLOPS, 1555 GB/s, 40-80 GB). If S0 shows the operator is f64-ALU-bound, a device change is worth more than every algorithmic lever in this document combined; if it is latency/occupancy-bound, it is still worth the bandwidth and SM count and it multiplies the ensemble R by 2.5-5x on memory alone. Question: is the project willing to move off the A5000 for sweep production, and does the hard rule 'the answer to native memory pressure is larger or multi-GPU hardware' extend to THROUGHPUT pressure?

SWEEP BUDGET — without this number, 'fast enough' is undefined and no optimisation can ever be declared DONE. Please state the target: how many cell types x how many cell states x how many replicates x how many physical seconds per run x acceptable wall per sweep. From that I can compute the required speedup and say honestly which combination of levers reaches it and which does not. Today's measured point is 0.05 s physical per 172 s wall, so the gap is currently ~4-6 orders of magnitude and the answer will certainly involve the surrogate — but the required factor determines whether S3+S7 alone could suffice for a reduced first sweep.

IS A HOST READBACK USED ONLY FOR LOOP CONTROL — no state read, no state mutation, bit-identical result — a violation of the zero-authoritative-GPU-to-CPU-roundtrip rule? This single ruling decides whether FIX1 can ship as written or must be re-implemented as a conditional graph. I recommend ruling it a violation anyway, because the conditional-graph implementation is strictly better (same skip, zero readback, fewer launches, guards still device-resident) — but the ruling is yours.

FIX2 CHANGES THE PRECONDITIONER on a solve that does NOT converge. A preconditioner change cannot move a CONVERGED fixed point, which is the usual reason preconditioner changes need no gate. But the production path is budget-exhausted (inner_iters = 400 = budget, inner_converged = False), so the emitted state IS preconditioner-dependent. Question: is a preconditioner change that alters a non-converged trajectory a gate-contract change requiring PI sign-off? The same question applies to S6's f32 preconditioner and is the reason I did not rank it higher.

IS A NEURAL SURROGATE ADMISSIBLE AT ALL under the fine-grained-mechanistic hard rule? A learned emulator is the most abstracted, most lumped object imaginable in a project whose first architectural principle is to prefer the mechanistic option even at higher cost. My proposed reconciliation is that the surrogate is not a runtime and not a model — it is a SEARCH POLICY over which native runs to perform, mechanically firewalled (package-level AST import ban, provenance gate blocking any production number without a native run id, native confirmation of every reported posterior point). But 'the surrogate explores, native decides' is a policy that needs your explicit ratification, not my inference, because it is the one place this track brushes against the project's founding rule.

DOES 'CO-LOCATION IS NEVER A CONNECTION' FORBID ensemble concatenation of independent cells into shared array sets even with a proven byte-identity block-diagonality gate? The letter of the rule is about physical connection within one cell; the spirit is that shared storage must never imply mechanical coupling. My reading is that a gated concatenation is admissible precisely because the gate proves non-coupling, and that stream-parallel separate cells (variant A) is the conservative fallback. Your call on whether the gate is sufficient.

PRECEDENT QUESTION on reduced precision: ac/solid/steric_warp.py:9-11,48-51 already builds the steric hash grid on an f32 copy of the positions, documented as safe because the grid only prunes far pairs while the force math stays f64. Is that (a) an accepted precedent that legitimises pruning-only reduced precision generally, or (b) something that needs retroactive gating? The answer sets the boundary for S6.

MAY I LAND S0 (profiler + throughput observable) NOW, ahead of the assembly tracks? It changes no physics, adds no constants, and is measurement-only — but it edits ac/cell/driver.py, which is feature-frozen (instrumentation is explicitly allowed, so I believe yes). The reason to do it now rather than after assembly is that every speedup estimate in this document is currently undecidable, and building the baseline incrementally as compartments land is far cheaper than reconstructing it cold at the end.

WHICH OBSERVABLE anchors the S7 dt-convergence plateau? A dt study needs one quantity to converge, and choosing it myself risks choosing one that is insensitive to dt and therefore produces a flat, vacuous plateau. I would propose the accepted-step force-balance residual plus one mechanical observable of the adherent configuration, but the choice is a measurement-protocol decision with gate consequences.
